_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4436 — the DELIVERED-PREVIEW half of `set-body --dry-run`. Separate spec because the axis needs a REAL process with a REAL stderr pipe on the BUILT bundle, which jest cannot provide (its axes mock process.stderr.write and process.exit). ⛔ This spec and its harness run LOCALLY and under the mutant driver, NOT in CI: the CLI jest job does not build dist, and the harness is not named `*-verify.{sh,py}` so verify-harness-runner does not sweep it either (harness-invocation-surface §A19 — naming that inapplicability out loud rather than leaving it to be read as an oversight). Same shape as get-body-9de09856.pipe.spec.json, which locked the sibling fix in #4434. Expectation written BEFORE the run, and the RED state was OBSERVED on the pre-fix bundle: PASS=5 FAIL=1, S1 delivered 65 536 of 605 709 bytes (89.2 % lost, tail marker absent) while S2 (the same preview through a FILE) was byte-identical to the computed expectation. S7 was added after round-1 review demonstrated by execution that dropping process.exit(0) trades the truncation for an EPIPE crash on an early-closing reader (origin/main rc=0 5/5 vs the naive fix rc=1 5/5); it is the axis that keeps the fix from being a net regression on its own headline scenario. The harness rebuilds by default so a mutated copy of the tree is measured, not a stale bundle.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/src/commands/set-body.ts

M1_process_exit_after_write._note: Restores the pre-fix pattern: process.exit(0) at the end of the success path. It does not wait for an asynchronous write to drain, and stderr IS asynchronous when it is a pipe — so the --dry-run preview is cut at the 64 KiB buffer. Everything else stays GREEN, and that is what proves S1 measures PIPE DRAINING rather than 'rebuilding the document at all': S2 (file redirect) and S5 (small preview) never reach the buffer, S3/S4/S6 read the ~120-byte stdout echo, which can never truncate.

M2_truncate_the_preview._note: Control that the preview axes are not vacuous: a mutant that shortens the preview ITSELF must redden the pipe axis (S1), the file-redirect control (S2) AND the small-body axis (S5), while the write path (S4), the no-write guarantee (S3) and the no-change notice (S6) stay GREEN. Without this mutant, S2/S5 would have no demonstrated red state and 'the expectation is right' would rest on a single green run.

M3_stdio_epipe_guard_removed._note: Removes the EPIPE guard that the exit-less success path requires. process.exit(0) used to terminate the process BEFORE the OS delivered the asynchronous EPIPE a closed reader causes; without the exit AND without this guard, that EPIPE is an unhandled 'error' event — an uncaught exception, rc=1 plus a stack trace — on the very scenario the truncation fix exists for (`--dry-run | less`, quit with q). Measured: origin/main rc=0 5/5, the naive exit-less fix rc=1 5/5. Only S7 reddens: the other axes read the stream to EOF, so they cannot model a reader that leaves.
